purpose: Collect georeferenced, instrumented observations that can validate specific Earth-site properties used in ANALOG-X. Field evidence does not validate Moon/Mars equivalence, resource abundance, landing safety or rover traversability.

no_fieldwork_without: protected-area and environmental clearance where applicable
site-specific risk assessment and weather review
named field lead, emergency contacts and communications plan
data_integrity: Record UTC timestamps and WGS84 coordinates with method and accuracy
Use unique station, photograph and sample identifiers
Preserve original media and unedited instrument exports
Maintain sample custody and permit restrictions
Do not promote an observation to independently_reviewed without an identified reviewer, review date and defined review scope
governance.access_note: Locations are approximate research areas only. This document does not authorize entry or travel. Obtain current local approvals and site-specific advice before a visit.

required_minimum: GNSS-enabled location recorder with stated accuracy
camera with original files and recorded bearings
field notebook or digital observation log
thermometer for air and/or surface readings with instrument ID
site map, communications and first-aid/emergency equipment appropriate to risk
optional_by_method: portable electrical-conductivity meter for authorized salinity screening
sample bags, labels, seals and chain-of-custody log
field_kit.calibration: Record instrument make/model/serial, calibration date or field-check procedure, units, precision and any known offsets. Do not enter a value as measured if the relevant instrument was not used.

candidate_campaigns.site_name: Chagai small salt playas near Nok Kundi
candidate_campaigns.research_question: What surface, crust, sediment and playa-margin characteristics are directly observable, and how do they vary from margin to interior?

station_design.purpose: Document fan/playa boundary, sediment transition and surface crust at a safe accessible margin
Capture repeatable surface texture and landform changes along a permitted transect

station_design.station_type: playa interior (only if permitted and safe)
station_design.purpose: Describe crust continuity, texture and surface condition; no subsurface inference

observations: geomorphic setting and boundary position
directly visible crust type, continuity and thickness only where naturally exposed
sediment grain size, sorting and clast description using a recorded method
surface and air temperature, humidity and wind with instrument IDs
electrical conductivity only if an authorized instrument and sampling method are available
geotagged photographs with bearings and scale reference
specific_limits: Approximate research AOI is not a surveyed playa boundary
Do not infer salt-resource volume, brine, subsurface water or mineral grade
Do not disturb or collect material without explicit permission

candidate_campaigns.research_question: Which basin-margin, playa-surface and drainage features are present at sampled locations, and what is directly observed versus inferred from regional imagery?

station_design.purpose: Record landform, sediment and drainage transition at an authorized accessible margin
Describe surface crust, moisture appearance, texture and vegetation without implying subsurface water
Document channel/fan material, sediment size and visible depositional features

observations: directly observed landform and drainage features
surface condition and moisture indicators with method and uncertainty
crust/sediment texture and grain-size description
vegetation cover at station scale as an observation, not a full-cover map
temperature, humidity and wind where measured
photographs and coordinate accuracy
specific_limits: Hydrological boundaries and intermittent activity require independent, time-stamped evidence
Do not interpret a single visit as seasonal hydrology
No claims of brine, water resources or unique evaporite deposits

candidate_campaigns.research_question: Can mapped volcanic units and alteration/weathering features be verified at accessible exposures, with lithology described by qualified field geologists?

station_design.purpose: Describe the exposed unit and record whether the outcrop matches published map terminology
Document observed contacts, mixed material and uncertainty without assuming continuity
Record visible feature and its context; specialist analytical work required for any mineral claim

observations: outcrop-scale lithology by qualified geologist
field photographs with scale, bearing and exposure context
weathering/alteration descriptions kept separate from interpretation
grain size, clast/support and structural observations where exposed
sample IDs only where permitted and with chain of custody
optional portable measurements with method, instrument and limitations
specific_limits: Published descriptions include agglomerate, tuff and andesitic lava; do not label the site a basaltic Mars match by assumption
No mineral identification or grade claim from visual inspection or spectral browse imagery
No sampling without permits and competent geological oversight

candidate_campaigns.research_question: How do glacier ice, debris cover, moraine and adjacent sediment appear at safely accessible observation points, and what limits remote-sensing interpretation?

station_design.purpose: Use remote photography and binocular/telephoto observation from a professionally assessed safe location
Describe debris cover, sediment and visible ice relation without approaching crevasse or unstable terrain
Document sediment and landform context at an approved stable location

observations: glacier/debris features from a safe assessed location
visible crevasse, avalanche, rockfall and meltwater hazards from distance
sediment and moraine descriptions at accessible stable ground
time-stamped photographs and station coordinates
weather and access constraints
specific_limits: No glacier-surface access without qualified glacier guides, a professional hazard assessment, rope/rescue capability and a specific expedition safety plan
Do not enter crevasse fields, unstable ice or avalanche terrain for this project
Terrestrial glacier ice is not evidence of lunar polar ice accessibility or equivalent thermal conditions

before_visit: station IDs and transects finalized by field lead
team roles and emergency plan recorded
after_visit: preserve original photos and instrument files
independent review before changing status to independently_reviewed
minimum_release_requirements.review_scope: Each review applies only to the observations and site properties actually inspected. It does not confer planetary-analog certification.

repository_workflow.explicit_note: The browser kit does not upload records. Export, preserve originals, review and commit through a controlled repository change.
